The styling that applies to a section.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|columnProperties|[[SectionColumnProperties](#schemasectioncolumnproperties)]|false|none|The section's columns properties. If empty, the section contains one column with the default properties in the Docs editor. A section can be updated to have no more than 3 columns. When updating this property, setting a concrete value is required. Unsetting this property will result in a 400 bad request error.|
|columnSeparatorStyle|string|false|none|The style of column separators. This style can be set even when there's one column in the section. When updating this property, setting a concrete value is required. Unsetting this property results in a 400 bad request error.|
|contentDirection|string|false|none|The content direction of this section. If unset, the value defaults to LEFT_TO_RIGHT. When updating this property, setting a concrete value is required. Unsetting this property results in a 400 bad request error.|
|defaultFooterId|string|false|none|The ID of the default footer. If unset, the value inherits from the previous SectionBreak's SectionStyle. If the value is unset in the first SectionBreak, it inherits from DocumentStyle's default_footer_id. This property is read-only.|
|defaultHeaderId|string|false|none|The ID of the default header. If unset, the value inherits from the previous SectionBreak's SectionStyle. If the value is unset in the first SectionBreak, it inherits from DocumentStyle's default_header_id. This property is read-only.|
|evenPageFooterId|string|false|none|The ID of the footer used only for even pages. If the value of DocumentStyle's use_even_page_header_footer is true, this value is used for the footers on even pages in the section. If it is false, the footers on even pages use the default_footer_id. If unset, the value inherits from the previous SectionBreak's SectionStyle. If the value is unset in the first SectionBreak, it inherits from DocumentStyle's even_page_footer_id. This property is read-only.|
|evenPageHeaderId|string|false|none|The ID of the header used only for even pages. If the value of DocumentStyle's use_even_page_header_footer is true, this value is used for the headers on even pages in the section. If it is false, the headers on even pages use the default_header_id. If unset, the value inherits from the previous SectionBreak's SectionStyle. If the value is unset in the first SectionBreak, it inherits from DocumentStyle's even_page_header_id. This property is read-only.|
|firstPageFooterId|string|false|none|The ID of the footer used only for the first page of the section. If use_first_page_header_footer is true, this value is used for the footer on the first page of the section. If it's false, the footer on the first page of the section uses the default_footer_id. If unset, the value inherits from the previous SectionBreak's SectionStyle. If the value is unset in the first SectionBreak, it inherits from DocumentStyle's first_page_footer_id. This property is read-only.|
|firstPageHeaderId|string|false|none|The ID of the header used only for the first page of the section. If use_first_page_header_footer is true, this value is used for the header on the first page of the section. If it's false, the header on the first page of the section uses the default_header_id. If unset, the value inherits from the previous SectionBreak's SectionStyle. If the value is unset in the first SectionBreak, it inherits from DocumentStyle's first_page_header_id. This property is read-only.|
|flipPageOrientation|boolean|false|none|Optional. Indicates whether to flip the dimensions of DocumentStyle's page_size for this section, which allows changing the page orientation between portrait and landscape. If unset, the value inherits from DocumentStyle's flip_page_orientation. When updating this property, setting a concrete value is required. Unsetting this property results in a 400 bad request error.|
|marginBottom|[Dimension](#schemadimension)|false|none|The bottom page margin of the section. If unset, the value defaults to margin_bottom from DocumentStyle. When updating this property, setting a concrete value is required. Unsetting this property results in a 400 bad request error.|
|marginFooter|[Dimension](#schemadimension)|false|none|The footer margin of the section. If unset, the value defaults to margin_footer from DocumentStyle. If updated, use_custom_header_footer_margins is set to true on DocumentStyle. The value of use_custom_header_footer_margins on DocumentStyle indicates if a footer margin is being respected for this section When updating this property, setting a concrete value is required. Unsetting this property results in a 400 bad request error.|
|marginHeader|[Dimension](#schemadimension)|false|none|The header margin of the section. If unset, the value defaults to margin_header from DocumentStyle. If updated, use_custom_header_footer_margins is set to true on DocumentStyle. The value of use_custom_header_footer_margins on DocumentStyle indicates if a header margin is being respected for this section. When updating this property, setting a concrete value is required. Unsetting this property results in a 400 bad request error.|
|marginLeft|[Dimension](#schemadimension)|false|none|The left page margin of the section. If unset, the value defaults to margin_left from DocumentStyle. Updating the left margin causes columns in this section to resize. Since the margin affects column width, it's applied before column properties. When updating this property, setting a concrete value is required. Unsetting this property results in a 400 bad request error.|
|marginRight|[Dimension](#schemadimension)|false|none|The right page margin of the section. If unset, the value defaults to margin_right from DocumentStyle. Updating the right margin causes columns in this section to resize. Since the margin affects column width, it's applied before column properties. When updating this property, setting a concrete value is required. Unsetting this property results in a 400 bad request error.|
|marginTop|[Dimension](#schemadimension)|false|none|The top page margin of the section. If unset, the value defaults to margin_top from DocumentStyle. When updating this property, setting a concrete value is required. Unsetting this property results in a 400 bad request error.|
|pageNumberStart|integer(int32)|false|none|The page number from which to start counting the number of pages for this section. If unset, page numbering continues from the previous section. If the value is unset in the first SectionBreak, refer to DocumentStyle's page_number_start. When updating this property, setting a concrete value is required. Unsetting this property results in a 400 bad request error.|
|sectionType|string|false|none|Output only. The type of section.|
|useFirstPageHeaderFooter|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether to use the first page header / footer IDs for the first page of the section. If unset, it inherits from DocumentStyle's use_first_page_header_footer for the first section. If the value is unset for subsequent sectors, it should be interpreted as false. When updating this property, setting a concrete value is required. Unsetting this property results in a 400 bad request error.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|columnSeparatorStyle|COLUMN_SEPARATOR_STYLE_UNSPECIFIED|
|columnSeparatorStyle|NONE|
|columnSeparatorStyle|BETWEEN_EACH_COLUMN|
|contentDirection|CONTENT_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED|
|contentDirection|LEFT_TO_RIGHT|
|contentDirection|RIGHT_TO_LEFT|
|sectionType|SECTION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|sectionType|CONTINUOUS|
|sectionType|NEXT_PAGE|

A StructuralElement describes content that provides structure to the document.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|endIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The zero-based end index of this structural element, exclusive, in UTF-16 code units.|
|paragraph|[Paragraph](#schemaparagraph)|false|none|A paragraph type of structural element.|
|sectionBreak|[SectionBreak](#schemasectionbreak)|false|none|A section break type of structural element.|
|startIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The zero-based start index of this structural element, in UTF-16 code units.|
|table|[Table](#schematable)|false|none|A table type of structural element.|
|tableOfContents|[TableOfContents](#schematableofcontents)|false|none|A table of contents type of structural element.|

<h2 id="tocS_SubstringMatchCriteria">SubstringMatchCriteria</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasubstringmatchcriteria"></a>
<a id="schema_SubstringMatchCriteria"></a>
<a id="tocSsubstringmatchcriteria"></a>
<a id="tocssubstringmatchcriteria"></a>

```json
{
  "matchCase": true,
  "text": "string"
}
```

A criteria that matches a specific string of text in the document.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|matchCase|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the search should respect case: - `True`: the search is case sensitive. - `False`: the search is case insensitive.|
|text|string|false|none|The text to search for in the document.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|tableStyle|[TableStyle](#schematablestyle)|false|none|The style of the table.|

```json
    "rowSpan": 0
  }
}
```

The contents and style of a cell in a Table.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|content|[[StructuralElement](#schemastructuralelement)]|false|none|The content of the cell.|
|endIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The zero-based end index of this cell, exclusive, in UTF-16 code units.|
|startIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The zero-based start index of this cell, in UTF-16 code units.|
|suggestedDeletionIds|[string]|false|none|The suggested deletion IDs. If empty, then there are no suggested deletions of this content.|
|suggestedInsertionIds|[string]|false|none|The suggested insertion IDs. A TableCell may have multiple insertion IDs if it's a nested suggested change. If empty, then this is not a suggested insertion.|
|suggestedTableCellStyleChanges|object|false|none|The suggested changes to the table cell style, keyed by suggestion ID.|
|tableCellStyle|[TableCellStyle](#schematablecellstyle)|false|none|The style of the cell.|

<h2 id="tocS_TableCellBorder">TableCellBorder</h2>

```json
{
  "color": {
    "color": {
      "rgbColor": {
        "blue": 0,
        "green": 0,
        "red": 0
      }
    }
  },
  "dashStyle": "DASH_STYLE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "width": {
    "magnitude": 0,
    "unit": "UNIT_UNSPECIFIED"
  }
}
```

A border around a table cell. Table cell borders cannot be transparent. To hide a table cell border, make its width 0.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|color|[OptionalColor](#schemaoptionalcolor)|false|none|The color of the border. This color cannot be transparent.|
|dashStyle|string|false|none|The dash style of the border.|
|width|[Dimension](#schemadimension)|false|none|The width of the border.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|dashStyle|DASH_STYLE_UNSPECIFIED|
|dashStyle|SOLID|
|dashStyle|DOT|
|dashStyle|DASH|

```json
    "index": 0,

  }
```

Location of a single cell within a table.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|columnIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The zero-based column index. For example, the second column in the table has a column index of 1.|
|rowIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|The zero-based row index. For example, the second row in the table has a row index of 1.|
|tableStartLocation|[Location](#schemalocation)|false|none|The location where the table starts in the document.|

The style of a TableCell. Inherited table cell styles are represented as unset fields in this message. A table cell style can inherit from the table's style.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backgroundColor|[OptionalColor](#schemaoptionalcolor)|false|none|The background color of the cell.|
|borderBottom|[TableCellBorder](#schematablecellborder)|false|none|The bottom border of the cell.|
|borderLeft|[TableCellBorder](#schematablecellborder)|false|none|The left border of the cell.|
|borderRight|[TableCellBorder](#schematablecellborder)|false|none|The right border of the cell.|
|borderTop|[TableCellBorder](#schematablecellborder)|false|none|The top border of the cell.|
|columnSpan|integer(int32)|false|none|The column span of the cell. This property is read-only.|
|contentAlignment|string|false|none|The alignment of the content in the table cell. The default alignment matches the alignment for newly created table cells in the Docs editor.|
|paddingBottom|[Dimension](#schemadimension)|false|none|The bottom padding of the cell.|
|paddingLeft|[Dimension](#schemadimension)|false|none|The left padding of the cell.|
|paddingRight|[Dimension](#schemadimension)|false|none|The right padding of the cell.|
|paddingTop|[Dimension](#schemadimension)|false|none|The top padding of the cell.|
|rowSpan|integer(int32)|false|none|The row span of the cell. This property is read-only.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|contentAlignment|CONTENT_ALIGNMENT_UNSPECIFIED|
|contentAlignment|CONTENT_ALIGNMENT_UNSUPPORTED|
|contentAlignment|TOP|
|contentAlignment|MIDDLE|
|contentAlignment|BOTTOM|

A mask that indicates which of the fields on the base TableCellStyle have been changed in this suggestion. For any field set to true, there's a new suggested value.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backgroundColorSuggested|boolean|false|none|Indicates if there was a suggested change to background_color.|
|borderBottomSuggested|boolean|false|none|Indicates if there was a suggested change to border_bottom.|
|borderLeftSuggested|boolean|false|none|Indicates if there was a suggested change to border_left.|
|borderRightSuggested|boolean|false|none|Indicates if there was a suggested change to border_right.|
|borderTopSuggested|boolean|false|none|Indicates if there was a suggested change to border_top.|
|columnSpanSuggested|boolean|false|none|Indicates if there was a suggested change to column_span.|
|contentAlignmentSuggested|boolean|false|none|Indicates if there was a suggested change to content_alignment.|
|paddingBottomSuggested|boolean|false|none|Indicates if there was a suggested change to padding_bottom.|
|paddingLeftSuggested|boolean|false|none|Indicates if there was a suggested change to padding_left.|
|paddingRightSuggested|boolean|false|none|Indicates if there was a suggested change to padding_right.|
|paddingTopSuggested|boolean|false|none|Indicates if there was a suggested change to padding_top.|
|rowSpanSuggested|boolean|false|none|Indicates if there was a suggested change to row_span.|


A StructuralElement representing a table of contents.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|content|[[StructuralElement](#schemastructuralelement)]|false|none|The content of the table of contents.|
|suggestedDeletionIds|[string]|false|none|The suggested deletion IDs. If empty, then there are no suggested deletions of this content.|
|suggestedInsertionIds|[string]|false|none|The suggested insertion IDs. A TableOfContents may have multiple insertion IDs if it is a nested suggested change. If empty, then this is not a suggested insertion.|

<h2 id="tocS_TableRange">TableRange</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematablerange"></a>
<a id="schema_TableRange"></a>
<a id="tocStablerange"></a>
<a id="tocstablerange"></a>

```json
{
  "columnSpan": 0,
  "rowSpan": 0,
  "tableCellLocation": {
    "columnIndex": 0,
    "rowIndex": 0,
    "tableStartLocation": {
      "index": 0,
      "segmentId": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

A table range represents a reference to a subset of a table. It's important to note that the cells specified by a table range do not necessarily form a rectangle. For example, let's say we have a 3 x 3 table where all the cells of the last row are merged together. The table looks like this: [ ] A table range with table cell location = (table_start_location, row = 0, column = 0), row span = 3 and column span = 2 specifies the following cells: x x [ x x x ]

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|columnSpan|integer(int32)|false|none|The column span of the table range.|
|rowSpan|integer(int32)|false|none|The row span of the table range.|
|tableCellLocation|[TableCellLocation](#schematablecelllocation)|false|none|The cell location where the table range starts.|

<h2 id="tocS_TextStyle">TextStyle</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematextstyle"></a>
<a id="schema_TextStyle"></a>
<a id="tocStextstyle"></a>
<a id="tocstextstyle"></a>

```json
{
  "backgroundColor": {
    "color": {
      "rgbColor": {
        "blue": 0,
        "green": 0,
        "red": 0
      }
    }
  },
  "baselineOffset": "BASELINE_OFFSET_UNSPECIFIED",
  "bold": true,
  "fontSize": {
    "magnitude": 0,
    "unit": "UNIT_UNSPECIFIED"
  },
  "foregroundColor": {
    "color": {
      "rgbColor": {
        "blue": 0,
        "green": 0,
        "red": 0
      }
    }
  },
  "italic": true,
  "link": {
    "bookmarkId": "string",
    "headingId": "string",
    "url": "string"
  },
  "smallCaps": true,
  "strikethrough": true,
  "underline": true,
  "weightedFontFamily": {
    "fontFamily": "string",
    "weight": 0
  }
}
```

Represents the styling that can be applied to text. Inherited text styles are represented as unset fields in this message. A text style's parent depends on where the text style is defined: * The TextStyle of text in a Paragraph inherits from the paragraph's corresponding named style type. * The TextStyle on a named style inherits from the normal text named style. * The TextStyle of the normal text named style inherits from the default text style in the Docs editor. * The TextStyle on a Paragraph element that's contained in a table may inherit its text style from the table style. If the text style does not inherit from a parent, unsetting fields will revert the style to a value matching the defaults in the Docs editor.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backgroundColor|[OptionalColor](#schemaoptionalcolor)|false|none|The background color of the text. If set, the color is either an RGB color or transparent, depending on the `color` field.|
|baselineOffset|string|false|none|The text's vertical offset from its normal position. Text with `SUPERSCRIPT` or `SUBSCRIPT` baseline offsets is automatically rendered in a smaller font size, computed based on the `font_size` field. Changes in this field don't affect the `font_size`.|
|bold|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the text is rendered as bold.|
|fontSize|[Dimension](#schemadimension)|false|none|The size of the text's font.|
|foregroundColor|[OptionalColor](#schemaoptionalcolor)|false|none|The foreground color of the text. If set, the color is either an RGB color or transparent, depending on the `color` field.|
|italic|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the text is italicized.|
|link|[Link](#schemalink)|false|none|The hyperlink destination of the text. If unset, there's no link. Links are not inherited from parent text. Changing the link in an update request causes some other changes to the text style of the range: * When setting a link, the text foreground color will be updated to the default link color and the text will be underlined. If these fields are modified in the same request, those values will be used instead of the link defaults. * Setting a link on a text range that overlaps with an existing link will also update the existing link to point to the new URL. * Links are not settable on newline characters. As a result, setting a link on a text range that crosses a paragraph boundary, such as `"ABC\n123"`, will separate the newline character(s) into their own text runs. The link will be applied separately to the runs before and after the newline. * Removing a link will update the text style of the range to match the style of the preceding text (or the default text styles if the preceding text is another link) unless different styles are being set in the same request.|
|smallCaps|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the text is in small capital letters.|
|strikethrough|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the text is struck through.|
|underline|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the text is underlined.|
|weightedFontFamily|[WeightedFontFamily](#schemaweightedfontfamily)|false|none|The font family and rendered weight of the text. If an update request specifies values for both `weighted_font_family` and `bold`, the `weighted_font_family` is applied first, then `bold`. If `weighted_font_family#weight` is not set, it defaults to `400`. If `weighted_font_family` is set, then `weighted_font_family#font_family` must also be set with a non-empty value. Otherwise, a 400 bad request error is returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|baselineOffset|BASELINE_OFFSET_UNSPECIFIED|
|baselineOffset|NONE|
|baselineOffset|SUPERSCRIPT|
|baselineOffset|SUBSCRIPT|

Unmerges cells in a Table.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tableRange|[TableRange](#schematablerange)|false|none|The table range specifying which cells of the table to unmerge. All merged cells in this range will be unmerged, and cells that are already unmerged will not be affected. If the range has no merged cells, the request will do nothing. If there is text in any of the merged cells, the text will remain in the "head" cell of the resulting block of unmerged cells. The "head" cell is the upper-left cell when the content direction is from left to right, and the upper-right otherwise.|

Updates the style of a range of table cells.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|string(google-fieldmask)|false|none|The fields that should be updated. At least one field must be specified. The root `tableCellStyle` is implied and should not be specified. A single `"*"` can be used as short-hand for listing every field. For example to update the table cell background color, set `fields` to `"backgroundColor"`. To reset a property to its default value, include its field name in the field mask but leave the field itself unset.|
|tableCellStyle|[TableCellStyle](#schematablecellstyle)|false|none|The style to set on the table cells. When updating borders, if a cell shares a border with an adjacent cell, the corresponding border property of the adjacent cell is updated as well. Borders that are merged and invisible are not updated. Since updating a border shared by adjacent cells in the same request can cause conflicting border updates, border updates are applied in the following order: - `border_right` - `border_left` - `border_bottom` - `border_top`|
|tableRange|[TableRange](#schematablerange)|false|none|The table range representing the subset of the table to which the updates are applied.|
|tableStartLocation|[Location](#schemalocation)|false|none|The location where the table starts in the document. When specified, the updates are applied to all the cells in the table.|

<h2 id="tocS_WeightedFontFamily">WeightedFontFamily</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaweightedfontfamily"></a>
<a id="schema_WeightedFontFamily"></a>
<a id="tocSweightedfontfamily"></a>
<a id="tocsweightedfontfamily"></a>

```json
{
  "fontFamily": "string",
  "weight": 0
}
```

Represents a font family and weight of text.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fontFamily|string|false|none|The font family of the text. The font family can be any font from the Font menu in Docs or from [Google Fonts] (https://fonts.google.com/). If the font name is unrecognized, the text is rendered in `Arial`.|
|weight|integer(int32)|false|none|The weight of the font. This field can have any value that's a multiple of `100` between `100` and `900`, inclusive. This range corresponds to the numerical values described in the CSS 2.1 Specification, [section 15.6](https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS21/fonts.html#font-boldness), with non-numerical values disallowed. The default value is `400` ("normal"). The font weight makes up just one component of the rendered font weight. A combination of the `weight` and the text style's resolved `bold` value determine the rendered weight, after accounting for inheritance: * If the text is bold and the weight is less than `400`, the rendered weight is 400. * If the text is bold and the weight is greater than or equal to `400` but is less than `700`, the rendered weight is `700`. * If the weight is greater than or equal to `700`, the rendered weight is equal to the weight. * If the text is not bold, the rendered weight is equal to the weight.|

<h2 id="tocS_WriteControl">WriteControl</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawritecontrol"></a>
<a id="schema_WriteControl"></a>
<a id="tocSwritecontrol"></a>
<a id="tocswritecontrol"></a>

```json
{
  "requiredRevisionId": "string",
  "targetRevisionId": "string"
}
```

Provides control over how write requests are executed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|requiredRevisionId|string|false|none|The optional revision ID of the document the write request is applied to. If this is not the latest revision of the document, the request is not processed and returns a 400 bad request error. When a required revision ID is returned in a response, it indicates the revision ID of the document after the request was applied.|
|targetRevisionId|string|false|none|The optional target revision ID of the document the write request is applied to. If collaborator changes have occurred after the document was read using the API, the changes produced by this write request are applied against the collaborator changes. This results in a new revision of the document that incorporates both the collaborator changes and the changes in the request, with the Docs server resolving conflicting changes. When using target revision ID, the API client can be thought of as another collaborator of the document. The target revision ID can only be used to write to recent versions of a document. If the target revision is too far behind the latest revision, the request is not processed and returns a 400 bad request error. The request should be tried again after retrieving the latest version of the document. Usually a revision ID remains valid for use as a target revision for several minutes after it's read, but for frequently edited documents this window might be shorter.|
